I replied to some of these. For media formats I’m still not quite sure what to do. Obviously we need to add those user agents ship today, but adding new formats seems dumb as it just increases the number of bytes that leak. Drawing a line in the sand and requiring explicit opt-in seems better, even if it means new formats have to be even better therefore.
That might also be a benefit as it would slow down adding new formats except when it really counts.

zcorpan: A sort of orthogonal question since one would want some level of defense-in-depth besides this[1], but do specs actually need to have the full range of HTML available to be doing XSS-like things?  (Are we including live code examples rather than just the code for something you could run elsewhere? / Putting them in iframes so the iframes get to run?)  Searchfox is using an allow-list for the PRs so it might just drop some stuff if that exists.

1: Arguably sandboxed iframes could be layered in.  I've used allow-same-origin without allow-scripts in the past for the Firefox OS email app where we also had allow-list sanitized the HTML already so that we could reach into the DOM for events but with a hard prevention on scripts even beyond the CSP.

One could also use or layer in a no-allow-same-origin but allow-scripts with sanitized contents where the only intended scripts are the support scripts for event hookup (which could also involve another iframe that does not have allow-scripts).
